issues.detail: The Greek 'εγενετο' (egeneto) is a past tense verb ('happened' or 'came to pass'). The Vietnamese translation 'đến cùng' (came to) treats 'lời Đức Chúa Trời' (the word of God) as the subject of a movement, but fails to capture the 'occurrence' aspect of the Greek verb. More importantly, the Greek indicates that the 'word of God happened/came to pass' *upon* John; the Vietnamese phrasing 'đến cùng Giăng' is slightly less precise regarding the manifestation of the word.
